subject: General Knowledge
topic: Prime Ministers & Presidents of India — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Which President of India holds the unique distinction of having served TWO consecutive full terms in office?

options.option_text: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, who served a single term from 1962 to 1967
Rajendra Prasad, who served two full terms from 1950 to 1962
Varahagiri Venkata Giri, who served a single term from 1969 to 1974
APJ Abdul Kalam, who served a single term from 2002 to 2007

questions.explanation: Rajendra Prasad was elected in 1952 and re-elected in 1957, serving as President from 1950 to 1962 — the only President to complete two consecutive terms. Radhakrishnan and VV Giri each served a single term; APJ Abdul Kalam also served only one term (2002–2007).

questions.stem: Which Prime Minister of India was the FIRST to be conferred the Bharat Ratna posthumously?

options.option_text: Jawaharlal Nehru, who received the Bharat Ratna in 1955 while in office
Lal Bahadur Shastri, awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1966 after his death in Tashkent
Indira Gandhi, who received the Bharat Ratna in 1971 while serving as PM
P. V. Narasimha Rao, awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024 decades after his tenure

questions.explanation: Lal Bahadur Shastri died on 11 January 1966 in Tashkent and was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously the same year — the first Prime Minister to receive this honour after death. Nehru received it in 1955 while alive; Indira Gandhi in 1971 while in office; PV Narasimha Rao was honoured much later in 2024, and is therefore not the first.

questions.stem: The national Emergency of June 1975 was proclaimed by the President of India under Article 352. Who held the office of President at that time?

options.option_text: Varahagiri Venkata Giri, who served as President from 1969 to 1974
Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, who served as President from 1974 to 1977
Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, who became President only in July 1977
Basappa Danappa Jatti, who served briefly as Acting President in 1977

questions.explanation: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed was President when the Emergency was proclaimed on 25–26 June 1975 on the advice of PM Indira Gandhi. VV Giri's term had already ended in August 1974. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy and BD Jatti both came to prominence in 1977 — after the Emergency was revoked.

questions.stem: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), guaranteeing 100 days of wage employment to rural households, was enacted during the tenure of which Prime Minister?

options.option_text: Atal Bihari Vajpayee, who led the NDA government from 1999 to 2004
Manmohan Singh, who led the UPA government when MGNREGA was passed in 2005
H. D. Deve Gowda, who headed the United Front government in 1996–1997
Rajiv Gandhi, who led the Congress government from 1984 to 1989

questions.explanation: MGNREGA was enacted in September 2005 under PM Manmohan Singh's UPA government and notified on 2 February 2006. Vajpayee's NDA lost the 2004 election before the Act was conceived as law. Deve Gowda and Rajiv Gandhi both preceded the UPA era by over a decade.

questions.stem: Pratibha Patil, India's first woman President (2007–2012), served as the Governor of which state immediately before her election to the Presidency?

options.option_text: Maharashtra, her home state where she held legislative roles for decades
Rajasthan, where she served as Governor from 2004 to 2007
Gujarat, a neighbouring state where she had no gubernatorial appointment
Madhya Pradesh, a central Indian state she did not serve as Governor of

questions.explanation: Pratibha Patil was the Governor of Rajasthan from 2004 to 2007 before being elected the 12th President of India in July 2007. Maharashtra is the most common wrong answer — she was an MLA and MP from Maharashtra but was never its Governor. Governors cannot serve in their home state under convention.

questions.stem: In April 1999, the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government lost the Lok Sabha confidence vote by the narrowest margin in Indian parliamentary history. What was the exact margin of defeat?

options.option_text: Lost by 2 votes — 268 in favour and 270 against the confidence motion
Lost by 1 vote — 269 in favour and 270 against the confidence motion
Lost by 3 votes — 267 in favour and 270 against the confidence motion
Lost by 5 votes — 265 in favour and 270 against the confidence motion

questions.explanation: The confidence motion on 17 April 1999 was defeated 270–269 — a margin of just ONE vote. This remains the slimmest defeat on a confidence motion in Indian parliamentary history. The fall of the government led to fresh elections in late 1999, in which the BJP-led NDA returned with a stronger majority.

questions.stem: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was elected the 6th President of India in 1977. What makes this Presidential election historically unique compared to all others in India?

options.option_text: He was the oldest person ever to be inaugurated as President of independent India
He was elected unopposed, the only uncontested Presidential election in India
He was the first President elected from the Telugu-speaking Andhra region of India
He was chosen directly by the Lok Sabha rather than by the full Electoral College

questions.explanation: Sanjiva Reddy was elected unopposed in 1977 — the sole instance of an uncontested Presidential election in India's history. Ironically, he had contested the 1969 election and lost to VV Giri. Option C is wrong because VV Giri, also of Telugu origin, preceded him. Option D is factually incorrect — Presidents are elected by the full Electoral College comprising Parliament and state legislatures, not by the Lok Sabha alone.
